sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.3% a year from $65.1 billion in FY2017 to $87.0 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F201].
The window is not smooth: FY2019 operating income fell 58.9% to $5.5 billion on an $8.3 billion impairment charge [F13][D97][X112].

That charge was a $6.8 billion goodwill write-down of the Shave Care reporting unit and a $1.6 billion Gillette intangible write-down, driven by currency devaluations, decelerating category growth and tougher competition [X109][P62].
FY2020 then rebounded with operating income up 186.2% to $15.7 billion, $8.3 billion of it from the base-period charge and the rest from sales growth and gross margin [F14][D148][P71].
The US was the growth engine for most of the window, contributing +4.0pp of FY2020 revenue growth and +2.2pp in FY2024 [D518][D530].
In FY2026 the pattern flipped: Non-US contributed +3.1pp of the 3.3% growth while the US added just +0.1pp [D511][D536][D457].
FY2026 net sales rose 3% on favorable foreign exchange of 2% and pricing of 1%, with unit volume and mix unchanged [P26].
Operating costs grew 2.1pp faster than revenue in FY2026, at 5.3% for cost of revenue and 5.5% for SG&A [D482][D472][D474].
Diluted EPS grew 1.7% against net income growth of 0.5%, helped by a 1.3% lower diluted share count [D461][D459][D476].
FY2026 operating margin of 22.7% sat 0.6pp above the 22.1% window median but 1.6pp below the FY2025 high of 24.3% [F30][D648][D647][D470].
The FY2026 decline came from cost of revenue (-1.0pp) and SG&A (-0.6pp), as gross margin fell on unfavorable category mix and marketing spending rose [D483][D485][P25][P5].
In FY2026 net margin of 18.4% sat 4.3pp below the 22.7% operating margin, with other income of $1.1 billion and a 20.8% tax rate narrowing the gap [F50][F30][X108][D443].
Other non-operating income rose $922 million to $1.1 billion on the prior-year Argentina translation charge and the Glad joint venture dissolution gain [X108][P24].
FY2026 operating cash flow of $19.6 billion was 1.22x net income, and free cash flow of $15.1 billion was 0.94x against a 1.02x window median [F80][F40][D444][F100][D445][D660].
Operating cash flow rose 10% as working capital generated $29 million, with payables adding $919 million offset by $641 million consumed by inventory [P3].
Free cash flow margin of 17.4% was near the 17.2% median, while capex at 5.1% of revenue ran 1.40x D&A [D441][D654][D440][D446].
Investing used $4.6 billion, primarily capital expenditures and net investment hedge settlements, partly offset by Glad proceeds [P2].
The company carries net debt of $24.2 billion, with net cash of -27.8% of revenue against a staples peer median of -1.0% (n=6) [D450][D451][D677].
That places it in the 33rd percentile on net cash, with a current ratio of 0.68x against a 0.72x window median [D676][F180][D663].
Buybacks and dividends of $15.3 billion were 100.7% of free cash flow in FY2026, down from 116.6% in FY2025 [D452][D453][D402].
Return on average equity of 30.1% trails the 44.4% peer median, reflecting the leveraged balance sheet [D456][D681].
The current ratio has been below 1.0x every year of the window and stood at 0.68x in FY2026 [F180][F171].
This is structural for a consumer staples company funded by supplier payables and short-term borrowings, not a liquidity signal on its own.
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2025 and FY2026, at 116.6% and 100.7% [D402][D453].
Payouts now consume essentially all free cash flow, leaving little cushion if capex keeps rising at 16.9% as it did in FY2026 [D464].
Whether FY2027 operating margin holds above the 22.1% window median or extends the 1.6pp FY2026 decline, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D648][D470].
Whether capex stays above the FY2026 5.1% of revenue or falls back toward the 4.0% FY2024 level [D440][D337].
Whether buybacks and dividends fall below the FY2026 100.7% of free cash flow or stay above it [D453].
